newsitem.title: JAPAN: NCB says can't accept Moody's downgrading.
newsitem.headline: NCB says can't accept Moody's downgrading.

text.p: Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB) said on Friday it could not accept the downgrading of its senior debt rating by Moody's Investors Service as it was based on a "misunderstanding".
It also said in a statement that it was regrettable that the credit rating agency had announced the downgrading without trying to confirm NCB's moves to work out a restructuring programme.
Earlier on Friday, Moody's said it had cut its rating for NCB bank debentures worth about 10 trillion yen to Ba1 from Baa3.
Moody's describes long-term debts with a "Ba" rating as being judged to have speculative elements because their future cannot be considered well-assured.
It is the first time Moody's has given a Ba1 senior debt rating to a Japanese bank.

NCB said in the statement that while Moody's attributed the downgrading to growing risks for holders of bank debentures issued by NCB, "we have to say that it is based on a complete misunderstanding, taking into account the environment surrounding our bank's business situation and other factors".
NCB added that it made public last month that it would work out a sweeping restructuring programme, but said Moody's has not tried to confirm the contents of the restructuring programme.

While Moody's also attributed the downgrading to uncertainty about official protection for holders of bank debentures issued by long-term credit banks, NCB said the bank has not been in a condition which requires official support.

NCB also said that the bank would clarify its management policy through announcing its earnings and restructuring programme and would call for appropriate assessments on NCB's senior debt, including debentures.
